To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the majority of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) cases show overexpression of fibroblast growth factor receptor 1 (FGFR1) in the cytoplamx and/or at the cell membrane.
fibronectin shows increased cytoplasm staining and/or abnormal membranous localization in the majority of hepatocellular carcinoma.
hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) shows abnormal expression of fibro-nectin protein.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the molecular biology of the hepatocyte.
the study of the expression of fibroblast growth factor (FGF) and fibroblast growth factors receptor (FGFR) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC).
the role of fibronectins in hepatocarcinogenesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
fibronectin is overexpressed in the majority of hepatocellular carcinoma, but the significance of this overexpression is uncertain.
fibronectin shows an abnormal staining pattern in hepatocellular carcinogenesis, and this abnormality may be a useful marker for the diagnosis and/or prognosis of HCC.
fibronectin staining is increased and/or shows an altered pattern in most hepatocellular carcinomata.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HCCs show abnormal expression of Fibronectin protein.
fibronectin is a marker of HCCs, and it may play a role in HCC pathogenesis.
fibronectin shows overexpression in the neoplasms, but the significance of this overexpression is uncertain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
fibronectin staining in HCC is not a good marker of fibrosis.
fibronectin is an important component of HCC.
HCCs show abnormal expression of the fibronectin extracellular matrix protein, and this may reflect a critical role for the protein in tumor genesis.
